name: Divya Desams — The Grand Five
theme: Five pillars of the 108 holy abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvar saints
description: The Divya Desams are the one hundred and eight abodes of Vishnu praised in the hymns of the twelve Alvar saints — a sacred geography sung into existence between the sixth and ninth centuries. This circuit gathers five of its greatest pillars. Srirangam stands first among all: the island temple of the reclining Ranganatha, the largest functioning temple complex in India and the heart of Sri Vaishnavism. On the seven hills of Tirumala waits Venkateswara, lord of the Kali age, whose shrine draws more pilgrims than any other on earth. At Srivilliputhur, the garland-poet Andal — the only woman among the Alvars — grew up in the temple garden and wed the god himself. Kanchipuram's Varadaraja Perumal anchors the great scholastic tradition of the north Tamil country, and at Thiruvananthapuram the serpent-couched Padmanabha owns an entire kingdom, whose kings ruled only as his servants. Together the five span three states and a millennium and a half of unbroken Vaishnava devotion — a lifetime pilgrimage in miniature.
